'''''Melaleuca rugulosa''''', commonly known as '''scarlet bottlebrush''', is a plant in the myrtle [[Family (taxonomy)|family]], [[Myrtaceae]] and is [[Endemism|endemic]] to [[South Australia]] and [[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] in [[Australia]]. (Some Australian state [[Herbarium|herbaria]] continue to use the name ''Callistemon rugulosus''.<ref name=Udovicic>{{cite journal|last1=Udovicic|first1=Frank|last2=Spencer|first2=Roger|title=New combinations in ''Callistemon'' (Myrtaceae)|journal=Muelleria|date=2012|volume=30|issue=1|pages=23–25|doi=10.5962/p.292240 |s2cid=251007557 |url=http://www.rbg.vic.gov.au/documents/Muelleria_30-1_3_Udovicic_Spencer.pdf|accessdate=16 July 2015}}</ref> ''Callistemon coccineus'' and ''Callistemon macropunctatus'' are older names for ''Callistemon rugulosus''.<ref name=ACRA>{{cite web|title=''Callistemon'' 'Harkness'|url=https://www.anbg.gov.au/acra/descriptions/acc028.html|publisher=Australian Cultivar Registration Authority|accessdate=20 July 2015}}</ref><ref name=ANPSA>{{cite web|title=Plant Name Changes|url=http://anpsa.org.au/changes.html|publisher=Australian Native Plants Society Australia|accessdate=20 July 2015}}</ref>) It is a shrub with an open straggly habit, stiff, sharply pointed leaves and bright red bottlebrush flowers tipped with yellow in summer.

==Description==
''Melaleuca rugulosa'' is a shrub growing to {{convert|5|m|ft|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} high with an open, straggling habit and peeling grey bark. Its leaves are arranged alternately and are {{convert|21-86|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long, {{convert|2.5-8.5|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} wide, flat, thick, rigid, narrow elliptic to egg-shaped with the narrower end near the base and have a sharp point. There is a mid-vein, marginal veins and 7–13 indistinct lateral veins. The young leaves and branches are often covered with dense, silky hairs.<ref name=Brophy>{{cite book|last1=Brophy|first1=Joseph J.|last2=Craven|first2=Lyndley A.|last3=Doran|first3=John C.|title=Melaleucas : their botany, essential oils and uses|date=2013|publisher=Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research|location=Canberra|isbn=9781922137517|page=309}}</ref><ref name=efloraSA>{{cite web|title=''Callistemon rugulosus''|url=http://www.flora.sa.gov.au/cgi-bin/speciesfacts_display.cgi?form=speciesfacts&name=Callistemon_rugulosus|publisher=Electronic Flora of South Australia|accessdate=31 March 2020}}</ref>

The flowers are a shade of red to purple, tipped with yellow and are arranged in spikes around the branches that continue to grow after flowering. The spikes are {{convert|40-65|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} in diameter and {{convert|50-80|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long with 18 to 60 individual flowers. The petals are {{convert|4.4-6.8|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long and fall off as the flower ages and there are 34-63 stamens in each flower. Flowering occurs from November to December, sometimes in other months and is followed by fruit that are woody [[Capsule (botany)|capsule]]s, {{convert|4.5-6.5|mm|in|sigfig=1|abbr=on}} long.<ref name="Brophy" /><ref name="efloraSA" />[[File:Callistemon macropunctatus.jpg|thumb|225px|Cultivated specimen in [[Palmetum of Santa Cruz de Tenerife]]]]

==Taxonomy and naming==
''Melaleuca rugulosa'' was first named in 2006 by [[Lyndley Craven]] in ''[[Novon]]'' when ''Callistemon rugulosus'' was transferred to the present [[genus]].<ref name=APNI>{{cite web|title=''Melaleuca rugulosa''|url=  https://biodiversity.org.au/boa/instance/apni/613704|publisher=APNI|accessdate=16 July 2015}}</ref><ref name=Novon>{{cite journal|last1=Craven|first1=Lyn A.|title=New Combinations in ''Melaleuca'' for Australian Species of ''Callistemon'' (Myrtaceae)|journal=Novon|date=2006|volume=16|issue=4|page=473|url=http://www.bioone.org/doi/abs/10.3417/1055-3177%282006%2916%5B468%3ANCIMFA%5D2.0.CO%3B2|accessdate=16 July 2015|doi=10.3417/1055-3177(2006)16[468:NCIMFA]2.0.CO;2|s2cid=84723155 |url-access=subscription}}</ref> It was first formally described in 1822 as ''Metrosideros rugulosa'' by [[Johann Heinrich Friedrich Link]] in ''[[Enumeratio Plantarum Horti Regii Berolinensis Altera]]''.<ref name=APNI-metr>{{cite web|title=''Metrosideros rugulosa''|url=  https://biodiversity.org.au/boa/instance/apni/473559|publisher=APNI|accessdate=16 July 2015}}</ref><ref name=Link>{{cite book|last1=Link|first1=Heinrich Friedrich|title=Enumeratio Plantarum Horti Regii Berolinensis Altera (Volume 2)|date=1822|location=Berlin|page=27|url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/item/1101#page/30/mode/1up|accessdate=3 September 2015}}</ref> The [[Botanical name|specific epithet]] (''rugulosa'') is from the [[Latin]] word ''[[wikt:ruga#Etymology 3|ruga]]'' meaning "crease" or "wrinkle"<ref name="RWB">{{cite book|last1=Brown|first1=Roland Wilbur|title=The Composition of Scientific Words|date=1956|publisher=Smithsonian Institution Press|location=Washington, D.C.|page =340}}</ref> but the reason for this naming is unclear.<ref name="Brophy" />

''Callistemon rugulosus'' is regarded as a synonym of ''Melaleuca rugulosa'' by the [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]].<ref name ="WCSP">{{cite web |url=http://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=31485 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221012202639/https://wcsp.science.kew.org/namedetail.do?name_id=31485 |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 12, 2022 |title=''Callistemon rugulosus'' |work=[[World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]] (WCSP) |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] }}</ref>

==Distribution and habitat==
This melaleuca occurs from the south east corner of South Australia including the [[Eyre Peninsula]] to western Victoria.<ref name="Brophy" /> It is found in mallee scrubs and low open woodland in the northern [[Grampians National Park|Grampians]], the [[Big Desert Wilderness Park|Big Desert]], the [[Little Desert National Park|Little Desert]], and the [[Mount Lofty Ranges]]. Within these areas it is found in sandy depressions and near watercourses in soils that are seasonally moist. It grows in [[shrubland]] and [[forest]] near swamps and watercourses.<ref name = costermans>{{cite book|author=Costermans, L.|title=Native Trees and Shrubs of South-eastern Australia|publisher=Rigby|location=Australia | year=1981 | isbn=072701403X}}</ref>
